whatChanged: NEW: Victory Capital agreed to buy First Eagle Investments for about $7bn -- $4bn cash, $2bn in new shares and $575m of assumed notes -- taking combined assets to roughly $571bn and acquiring First Eagle's $41bn CLO and alternative-credit platform (vctr-first-eagle-acquisition)

NEW: Alimentation Couche-Tard formally opened its PLN 32.00-a-share voluntary tender for all of Zabka Group, valuing Poland's largest convenience retailer at about PLN 32.6bn (~$8.7bn) with 57% of the register already committed by hard irrevocables (zab-couchetard-tender-offer)

NEW: SK Innovation will absorb listed battery-separator subsidiary SK IE Technology at 0.117454 SK Innovation shares per SKIET share effective 1 January 2027, targeting ~KRW60bn of annual cost savings; SK Innovation fell as much as 16% (sk-innovation-skiet-merger)

NEW: Nvidia paid Poolside $6bn for a non-exclusive licence to its 'Model Factory' training stack plus $1bn of equity at a $12bn pre-money valuation, and hired the 109 engineers who built it (nvda-poolside-model-factory-license)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsor-, sovereign-, cooperative- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names off public markets, and the pipeline is filling at both ends of the size range. Unresolved at the top end: Silver Lake is in talks to take Workday private at a ~$43bn market value (wday-silverlake-takeover-talks), KKR has an unsolicited ~$9bn, $42.50-a-share approach on the table for utility group UGI (ugi-kkr-takeover-bid), and WSP Global will file an offer memorandum with the Dutch AFM by 15 October to press a twice-rejected EUR51.50-a-share bid for Arcadis (arcad-wsp-takeover-bid). Below that, Abu Dhabi's L'IMAD is offering Dh6.25 a share for the ~24.6% of AD Ports Group its ADQ subsidiary does not hold (adports-limad-takeover-bid), Madrid-listed Deoleo has drawn rival cash offers from Dcoop at EUR470m and Coricelli at EUR500m -- the Italian bidder now demanding exclusivity and setting a 31 August lapse date (ole-dcoop-takeover-bid, ole-coricelli-takeover-bid), Trian is assembling co-investors behind a take-private of Wendy's (wen-trian-takeover-bid), InMode's special committee is free to act again now that the Haifa court has thrown out Steel Partners' injunction request (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), and JBS has proposed taking the ~18% of Pilgrim's Pride it does not own in an all-stock swap worth about $28.50 a share (ppc-jbs-minority-buyout). Two approaches have gone over the board or the register directly: Curaleaf's hostile tender for Aurora Cannabis runs to 1 December, with Aurora's special committee telling holders to take no action (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid), and Couche-Tard's PLN 32.00-a-share tender for Zabka opened on 26 August with 57% of the shares locked up by irrevocables and a squeeze-out and Warsaw delisting intended above 95% (zab-couchetard-tender-offer). Already signed or cleared: Two Harbors has final regulatory approval for its $12.00-a-share all-cash sale to privately held CrossCountry Mortgage (two-crosscountry-acquisition), Francisco Partners' $650m deal for Weave Communications (weav-francisco-partners-take-private), Thoma Bravo's $4bn+ deal for Accelerant (arx-thoma-bravo-take-private), Bernhard Capital's $43-a-share deal for Bowman (bwmn-bernhard-capital-takeover) and Blackstone Infrastructure's Safe Harbor buying MarineMax at $53 a share (hzo-safe-harbor-acquisition).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the constraint has narrowed to energised power rather than plans for it -- which is now pulling in the regulated utilities themselves: KKR's unsolicited ~$9bn approach for UGI's gas and electric utility, midstream and propane franchise is explicitly framed against data-center load growth (ugi-kkr-takeover-bid). The Ohio megaproject remains the clearest single example: Nvidia's backstop for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike campus is firm at up to $105bn of credit for the first 4.25GW, with an option covering a further 3.75GW (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and Nvidia has separately put $1.5bn of equity into developer SB Energy, which with SoftBank plans at least 10GW of new generation, a 9.2GW on-site gas plant costing ~$33bn and $4.2bn of Ohio grid investment (nvda-sbenergy-investment). Elsewhere Core Scientific paid ~$444m to take ~440MW of in-service, grid-connected Oklahoma capacity off a rival miner and push its Muskogee campus toward 1.5GW of AI colocation (corz-polaris-acquisition). How the build gets funded is the other half of the story, and the debt stacks keep getting larger: Nvidia has signed MOUs with six of the largest private-capital pools to mobilise over $500bn of third-party financing (nvda-compute-financing-platforms), Broadcom is sounding lenders for more than $60bn -- potentially $70-80bn -- against a chip-leasing vehicle aimed at over 20GW of frontier-lab compute by 2028 (avgo-anthropic-chip-financing), and Intel is selling $15bn of new stock to fund fab capex (intc-equity-offering-2026). On the equipment side Madison Air is paying $5.4bn for ebm-papst's fans and motor systems partly for the data-center cooling opportunity (mair-ebmpapst-acquisition); at the silicon layer Marvell has locked Google into a multi-year custom-chip programme for the TPU ecosystem (mrvl-google-tpu-partnership), Sony and TSMC are putting JPY747bn into a Kumamoto image-sensor fab (sony-tsmc-image-sensor-jv), and Micron is committing $10bn over a decade to a Boise foundational-research hub (mu-research-labs-investment) while SK hynix returns a record KRW40trn of the HBM windfall to shareholders rather than adding a third leg of capacity (skhynix-buyback-cancellation-2026).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being resolved by judges, regulators and shareholder ballots, in both directions. Paramount Skydance has satisfied every regulatory condition in its Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement, yet still cannot close until five days after a 12-day antitrust trial set for 2 March 2027 -- and the negotiated way out has broken down, with California AG Rob Bonta cancelling the settlement meeting and accusing Paramount of leaking and misrepresenting the previous session, leaving the $1.88bn bond demand and the $7m-a-day ticking fee from 30 September as the live pressure points (psky-wbd-acquisition). Delaware's Chancery Court has voided Verisk's walk-away from its $2.35bn AccuLynx purchase, ordering it to try again while the FTC review that triggered the termination is still unfinished (vrsk-acculynx-acquisition). Western Union's Intermex deal cleared New York's DFS on 14 August only for California's DFPI to suspend its own approval extension the day before, and the parties are still working to get it reinstated (imxi-westernunion-acquisition). Gates keep opening as well: Real's arrangement with RE/MAX cleared the Supreme Court of British Columbia and closed on 24 August, with Real REMAX Group trading on Nasdaq from the 25th (reax-remax-combination), Deutz's extraordinary general meeting backed the capital increase behind its EUR1.6bn FFG purchase with 99.7% in favour after an unconditional Bundeskartellamt clearance (dez-ffg-acquisition), Two Harbors received the last regulatory approval for its sale to CrossCountry Mortgage (two-crosscountry-acquisition), the Haifa court denied Steel Partners' injunction request in its entirety, releasing InMode's special committee to rule on the competing buyout bids (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), and California's PUC signed off on Charter-Cox as the final clearance needed, letting a $34.5bn merger close fifteen months after it was struck (chtr-cox-acquisition).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing, equity and exclusivity remain the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and the entanglement now runs in both directions. Nvidia's OpenAI backstop is a firm commitment of up to $105bn against the first 4.25GW of the Ohio campus rather than an open-ended guarantee over the whole 10GW project (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), and alongside it Nvidia has taken a $1.5bn equity stake in campus developer SB Energy that makes it the sole supplier of compute on the site it is financing (nvda-sbenergy-investment) -- the circularity critics object to, written into the cap table. It now extends past financing into capability: Nvidia has paid Poolside $6bn to license the 'Model Factory' training stack behind its Laguna models, put $1bn of equity into the startup at a $12bn pre-money valuation and hired the 109 engineers who built it, so the chip vendor is buying the method its own customers use to train (nvda-poolside-model-factory-license). Broadcom has taken the financing trade further than anyone: it is seeking more than $60bn of debt for a vehicle that buys Broadcom's own custom chips and leases them to Anthropic and potentially OpenAI, with Broadcom guaranteeing part of the senior tranche, so it would be booking chip revenue against paper it stands behind itself (avgo-anthropic-chip-financing). The syndicated version keeps scaling too: the six-firm compute-financing platforms are designed to lend against Nvidia's own GPUs so labs, enterprises and clouds can afford to buy them, moving the credit risk to Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR rather than carrying it in-house (nvda-compute-financing-platforms). Marvell has inverted the trade, handing Google a warrant over up to $12.2bn of its own stock -- vesting only as Google buys chips -- to anchor a custom-silicon programme for the TPU ecosystem, so the customer ends up owning the supplier rather than the other way round (mrvl-google-tpu-partnership).

themes.label: Asset managers buying scale and product lines rather than building them
themes.note: Two live deals show listed asset managers concluding that the capabilities the market now pays for are quicker to buy than to build. Victory Capital is paying about $7bn -- $4bn cash, $2bn in new shares and $575m of assumed notes -- for First Eagle Investments, taking combined assets to roughly $571bn and, more to the point, acquiring First Eagle's $41bn CLO and alternative-credit platform to serve as the enlarged group's alternatives arm (vctr-first-eagle-acquisition). Goldman Sachs is paying as much as $2.25bn in cash and equity for NEOS Investments and its 19 options-income ETFs with about $30bn of assets, buying a derivative-income and crypto-income ETF franchise it has no organic equivalent to (gs-neos-acquisition). In both cases the target is a fee-rate-defensible product line rather than plain AUM, and the buyer is a manager whose core business faces index-driven fee compression.
